newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Eurobourse gains eroded by volatile Wall St.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Eurobourse gains eroded by volatile Wall St.

text.p: European stocks were dragged down in late trading on Thursday by a volatile Wall Street which quickly shed early gains in a bout of profit-taking.
On currency markets, the dollar ended the European day up on the mark and yen as European leaders moved closer to reaching an agreement on a budgetary stability pact this weekend.

European bourses had an unsettled day, with most seeing their gains eroded at the close after spurting forward when weaker-than-expected U.S. retail sales figures allayed fears of an imminent rise in interest rates.
Nervous investors throughout the day kept a wary eye on New York where the Dow Industrial average has risen nearly 30 percent this year. Many believed a downturn was overdue.
So when Wall Street, which made a positive start on the data showed subdued inflationary pressures, suddenly turned sour and fell, European bourses got the jitters.
London, one of the strongest climbers and up 0.7 percent at one point, saw its advance eaten away and ended the day barely in the plus column.
"Until Wall Street upset us we were doing all right," said one senior sales trader. "Wall Street is calling the tune and if it deteriorates further we will do the same."
"I think the whole thing is very fragile and I think it's going to continue that way until things sort themselves out," said the head of equity trading at one major U.S. investment bank in London.
After rising 27 points at one stage, the FTSE 100 closed just 8.2 points higher at 3,990.7. British Gas, B.A.T and AB Foods were among the biggest gainers as investors went year-end bargain-hunting.
In Frankfurt, the IBIS index that measures computerised trading climbed by 0.7 percent after the U.S. data eased interest rate fears but slipped back to show a gain of only 0.4 at the finish.
Floor trade, which ended before the figures were issued, closed with a gain of 0.2 percent.
In Paris, stocks made a modest advance by midafternoon retreated to a slight loss at the finish.
On the currency front, the dollar ended the European session comfortably above 1.54 marks and 113 yen as the prospects for agreement on an EU stability pact improved.

The dollar's role as a safe haven currency would be enhanced once the mark is merged into the proposed single European currency and agreement on the stability pact is seen as paving the way for the launch of monetary union.
"The comments we've been seeing throughout the morning make it more likely that we will see agreement on a stability pact at the weekend," said Teis Knuthsen, economist at First Chicago.
But the U.S. currency slipped from its best levels against the mark towards the end of the day, caught in the downdraft blowing through the bourses on both sides of the Atlantic.
"The dollar is trying to push higher but the market is very thin and lacking any momentum," said a Swiss bank dealer.
CURRENCIES
The dollar was quoted at 113.41 yen and 1.5425 marks against 112.92 and 1.5412 in late European business on Wednesday.
STOCK MARKETS
The FTSE 100 index of leading British shares ended 8.2 points higher at 3,990.7.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 1.17 at 2,212.11.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 6.03 at 2,847.08.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold ended at $368.45 an ounce, after fixing in the afternoon at $368.60 and Wednesday's close of $368.65. Silver was at $4.82 in late trade, down one cent.
